findings.claim: The res.file/res.download root decision says the root is 'the canonical parent directory of the file the app named', which can be read in two ways. One is canonical(file.getAbsoluteFile().getParentFile()). The other is canonical(file).getParentFile(). Under the second reading, a named file that is a symbolic link to a target with the same name (for example a.pdf -> /x/a.pdf) passes the D-270 component check, because canonical(file) equals root + name. The decision's own rule ('the file itself must be ... not a symbolic link') then silently fails.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the root is the canonical form of the named file's absolute parent (file.getAbsoluteFile().getParentFile().getCanonicalFile()), resolved before the file itself, and add a res.file test with a same-name symbolic link.

findings.claim: D-260 says every non-GET/HEAD request to a static-only path gets 405 with 'Allow: GET, HEAD', and the OPTIONS decision extends this. But the router's first result, unsupported method (an unknown token, or TRACE/CONNECT while disabled), is answered with 501 before any path lookup, so the request never reaches the static fallback. Neither D-260 nor the wave decisions say that 501 comes first. An implementer could therefore move static resolution ahead of it, or write a T27/T29 test that expects 405 for 'FOO /index.html'.
findings.suggested_fix: In the OPTIONS/405 decision, add that an unsupported or disabled method keeps the dispatcher's 501, and that D-260's 405 applies to recognised methods only. Record this in docs/api/static.md.

findings.claim: The method-mismatch decision says that 'Between equally valid options the decision follows ... the behaviour an Express user expects'. Express routes are method-specific, though, so with app.post('/login') plus express.static (or an SPA catch-all), GET /login falls through and serves the file or index.html. Under the decision it gets 405 instead. The choice is valid under D-259 ('same path'), but it is the opposite of Express, and SPA deep links that share a path with a POST handler break. The stated tie-break rule and the decision contradict each other.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the decision, but have docs/api/static.md (and express-migration.md) state the divergence from Express explicitly, with the workaround (register app.get for that path). Alternatively let GET/HEAD METHOD_MISMATCH fall through to a static file when one exists.
